messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text:
This is based on an urban American school district. Europe or else where in the world might be different. I averaged the numbers. 

Primary schools typically holds 2-3,000 students. 
High schools around 4-5,000 students
Universities around 40,000.

messages.author: FikusMikus
messages.text: Multiples of 5000 would work best for the purposes of the game imo

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text: No we need to build more primary schools per high-school. There are usually 2 or 3 primary schools feeding into a middle/high school.

messages.author: 𝕿𝖍𝖊_𝖐𝖆𝖎𝖘𝖊𝖗
messages.text: Holy, yall have those biggass schools there?

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text:
We have towns that merge all grades into one school. Depends on the size of the town and cities. 

New York City for example has hundreds of primary schools and like 40 high schools.

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text: While my local town has 4 primary schools, 1 junior high and 1 high school.

messages.author: 𝕿𝖍𝖊_𝖐𝖆𝖎𝖘𝖊𝖗
messages.text: I never saw schools with more than 3k students in Italy

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text: Then if you go to another town near us, they have 1 primary school and send their higher education students to the city high school. Us.

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text: Our local university houses nearly 60,000 now.

messages.author: FikusMikus
messages.text: How does it benefit the gameplay in this instance

messages.author: Unknown Identity
messages.text:
Because it gives us stuff to build and not just copy builds from province to province which is boring. 

We can tailor builds now.

messages.author: 𝕿𝖍𝖊_𝖐𝖆𝖎𝖘𝖊𝖗
messages.text: I hope nobody gets offended by my statement

messages.author: AndyTheHusky
messages.text: Have an idea on making different sizes of school as well as schools that serve 2 levels at once
